summary: E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Wesley College, University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he served as principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Eberhard Fischer is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Basel. He served as Director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and later as Secretary General of the Swiss-Liechtenstein Foundation for Archaeological Research Abroad.

Eberhard Sandschneider is a sinologist who studied at Saarland University. He served as Professor of International Relations at Mainz (1995–1998), Managing Director at the Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and "Otto-Wolff-Direktor" at the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader worked in linguistics, studying at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the universities of Zurich (1863–1870), Giessen (1870–1873), Jena (1873–1875), and Berlin (1875–1908).

Edeltraud Harzer works in Indology and philosophy, having studied at the University of Prague, the University of Washington, and under Shrinarayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana University, and UT Austin.
Edgar H. Sturtevant was a linguist who studied at Illinois College and Indiana University. He held academic positions at Columbia University (~1908–1920) and Yale University (~1923–1943).

Edgar Thurston, a scholar of history and archaeology, studied at Eton College and King's College London (~1874–1877). He served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai, from around 1885 to 1908.

Edith Wyschogrod was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned degrees from Hunter College and Columbia University. She served as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.
Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. Around 1989, he held faculty posts at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, completing a PhD under Kuno Fischer at Heidelberg. He was a professor at Freiburg (1885–1893), Fribourg (1894–1898), and Würzburg (~1893–1904), and founded the Archiv für Religionswissenschaft.

Edmund Husserl was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt, Berlin, Vienna, and Halle. He held academic posts at the universities of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1901), Göttingen (1901–1916), and Freiburg (1916–1928).

Edmund Leach was an anthropologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at Clare College, Cambridge, and the LSE. He was a lecturer at the LSE (~1947–1953), professor at Cambridge (1953–1978), and provost of King's College, Cambridge (1966–1979).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indology scholar who graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886. He later pursued his studies under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Böhmer was a linguist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1847–1851). He later held posts at Halle-Wittenberg from 1859 to 1872 and at the University of Strasbourg from around 1872 to 1879.

Eduard Erkes was a sinologist who studied at the University of Leipzig under August Conrady. He held academic posts at the University of Berlin and the University of Leipzig (~1917–1958), where he succeeded Conrady.

Eduard Hermann was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Jena under Berthold Delbrück. He held posts at Kiel University (1913), Goethe University Frankfurt (1914), and served as Professor at the University of Göttingen (1917–1937).

Eduard Müller was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who completed an Inauguraldissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1872–1874). He served as a professor at the University of Bern from around 1886 to 1908.

Eduard Röer was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Johann Friedrich Herbart and Franz Bopp. He held posts at the East India Company (~1839–1858) and The Asiatic Society, serving as librarian and head of its linguistic department.

Eduard Sachau was an Orientalist who studied under Theodor Nöldeke, Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held professorships at the University of Vienna (1869) and the University of Berlin (from 1876), later directing the Seminar for Oriental Languages (1887).
